cases.script:
# GS-014: Release and recapture ammonia inside one closed system
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NH4Cl 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
measure v1 pressure
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
measure v1 pressure
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
measure v1 ph
measure v1 pressure
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Base favours NH3; subsequent acid returns nitrogen toward ammonium and lowers its gas-phase share without removing total nitrogen.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Track NH3 gas separately from ammonium and dissolved ammonia.
Nitrogen is conserved through the closed acid–base cycle.

original_limitations: Neutralisation heat affects pressure; gas-species accounting is essential.

cases.script:
# GS-018: Recover captured carbon from an isolated carbonate solid
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 Ca(OH)2 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
add v1 CO2 0.0005mol
inspect v1
new
filter v1 v2
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.003mol
measure v1 pressure
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Captured carbonate carbon should remain with the isolated solid and reappear as CO2/dissolved carbon on acidification; uncaptured carbon stays in the earlier liquid/gas accounts.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Quantify carbon in the first solid before assigning recaptured gas to it.
Sum carbon over both vessels and any boundary transfer during filtration.

original_limitations: Filtration and resealing may alter headspace inventory; the carbon ledger, not pressure alone, establishes recovery.

cases.script:
# KI-002: Removing a solid catalyst interrupts an ongoing reaction
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 H2O2 0.001mol
add v1 MnO2 0.001g
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 H2O2 0.001mol
add v2 MnO2 0.001g
wait 10s
new
filter v1 v3
inspect
wait 60s
inspect
cases.original_forecast: The catalyst-free filtrate should consume less additional peroxide than the unfiltered control, after correcting for their inventories at filtration.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Record the post-filtration starting peroxide in v3.
Distinguish slowed uncatalysed reaction from a claim of absolutely zero decomposition.

original_limitations: Any catalyst transfer or dissolved catalytic species would confound ideal physical removal.

cases.script:
# SE-009: Recover three physical fractions from an immiscible liquid–solid mixture
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 NaCl 0.001mol
add v1 hexane 20mL
add v1 SiO2 1g
new
drain v1 v2
new
filter v1 v3
inspect
cases.original_forecast: A lower aqueous fraction, an organic liquid fraction and an insoluble solid residue should be distinguishable, subject to the operators’ actual phase semantics.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Identify the composition of each destination rather than assigning it from vessel number.
Close water, hexane, salt and silica balances across all three vessels.

original_limitations: Interfacial trapping, emulsions and solid entrainment may be outside the ideal model.

cases.script:
# TC-002: Neutralisation heat is limited by the smaller reagent budget
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
new
add v2 water 50mL
add v2 HCl 0.002mol
new
add v3 water 50mL
add v3 NaOH 0.0005mol
new
add v4 water 50mL
add v4 NaOH 0.0005mol
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
measure v3 thermometer
measure v4 thermometer
decant v3 v1 1
decant v4 v2 1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
measure v1 calorimeter
measure v2 calorimeter
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Both mixtures can neutralise approximately 0.0005 mol of hydroxide, so the neutralisation contribution should be similar rather than doubled. The second mixture retains more excess acid.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Calculate temperature changes against each pair of measured pre-mixing temperatures and heat capacities.
Confirm the same hydroxide consumption but different residual acidity.

original_limitations: Dilution heat and different initial solution temperatures can affect raw temperature rises; raw final temperatures are not reaction heats.

cases.script:
# TC-009: Equal neutralisation extent, different thermal mass
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 25mL
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 HCl 0.001mol
new
add v3 water 25mL
add v3 NaOH 0.001mol
new
add v4 water 100mL
add v4 NaOH 0.001mol
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
measure v3 thermometer
measure v4 thermometer
decant v3 v1 1
decant v4 v2 1
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
measure v1 calorimeter
measure v2 calorimeter
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Both arms can neutralise 0.001 mol, but the less dilute arm should show the larger mixing-corrected temperature rise because it has a smaller thermal mass.

original_acceptance_checks.criterion: Compare heat-capacity-weighted pre-mixing baselines with final temperatures.
Distinguish approximately equal neutralisation energy from unequal temperature changes; do not demand an exact fourfold ratio.

original_limitations: Different concentrations introduce activity and dilution-enthalpy effects; total solution heat capacities are not exactly proportional to water volume.
